observation_kind: targeted current official polygon-topology/capture, Planning parameter, retired-25cm-LIDAR and Terrain-50 GML/metadata checks; not independent bulk HTTP fetches
rules: The National Polygon Dataset contains gaps, slivers, underlaps and overlaps; many are genuine and acceptable.
Small gaps and overlaps are documented dataset inconsistencies.
A technical overlap can arise from mapping inconsistency and does not itself describe a real title conflict.
An actual overlap is where two or more registered titles include the same land or property.
For index polygons, topology describes how polygons relate to and interact with one another.
Registrations at different floor levels can legitimately create overlapping polygons.
Different strata can legitimately create overlapping polygons.
Different tenures and classes of title can legitimately create overlapping polygons.
A caseworker can classify an acceptable referred overlap and allow it to remain.
Illegal overlaps are overlaps that should not exist in the dataset.
A referred index-polygon overlap can be investigated by a caseworker.
Where registered extents genuinely overlap, HMLR has limited power to amend them without an application.
Overlaps below 0.5 square metres are not referred for remedial action.
Very small overlaps may be too small to resolve satisfactorily with the mapping toolset.
The registration process considers adjoining registrations.
Minor polygon discrepancies should be resolved where titles are intended to adjoin.
Some registered titles are correctly non-adjoining, so their index polygons need not touch.
An index polygon represents title extent but must not be relied on as the exact registered extent.
An index polygon may be the same size, larger or smaller than the extent on the title plan.
Historic index polygons were manually captured on Ordnance Survey county-series sheets.
Historic index polygons were manually captured on national-grid sheets.
Historic index polygons were also captured from parcels books.
HMLR completed conversion of about 19 million paper index polygons to vector polygons in February 2004.
The vectorised polygons were mapped against Ordnance Survey Land-Line.
The conversion programme used temporary pictorial capture practices to complete the work efficiently.
During that temporary practice, title plans were seldom used to validate indexed extent.
HMLR's Positional Accuracy Improvement programme ran from 2005 to 2008.
Many affected polygons were moved automatically in sympathy with Ordnance Survey mapping.
Polygons outside automatic criteria were manually compared with title plans.
Almost 14 million index polygons passed through the Quality Improvement Flowline from around 2009.
The Quality Improvement Flowline resolved some minor overlaps.
The Quality Improvement Flowline automatically matched extents and reconciled polygons with title plans.
HMLR receives a daily change-only update of Ordnance Survey MasterMap.
That daily OSMM feed is used for new index polygons and title plans rather than routine review of existing registrations.
Existing index polygons are updated when relevant title activity or an adjoining title requires change.
Large-scale source mapping is captured at 1:1,250 in urban areas.
Large-scale source mapping is captured at 1:2,500 in semi-urban and rural areas.
Large-scale source mapping is captured at 1:10,000 in mountain and moorland areas.
HMLR index polygons are captured in British National Grid.
Indicative Extent is the most common current-practice feature type.
Exaggerated extents are used so narrow registered areas can be represented with at least one metre width.
Former gridding practice could split features at sheet joins, creating separate polygon identifiers.
The Planning Data API is in beta and may change for production integrations.
The q parameter searches by postcode or Unique Property Reference Number.
The typology parameter accepts multiple typology values.
The dataset parameter accepts multiple dataset values.
organisation_entity filters entities managed by one or more organisation identifiers.
The entity parameter filters by one or more entity numbers.
The curie parameter filters by one or more CURIE identifiers.
The prefix parameter filters by one or more prefixes.
The reference parameter filters by one or more source references.
The period parameter controls whether current or all entries are returned.
Start-date filtering can use separate year, month and day components.
Start-date components are interpreted using start_date_match.
End-date filtering can use separate year, month and day components.
End-date components are interpreted using end_date_match.
Entry-date filtering can use separate year, month and day components.
Entry-date components are interpreted using entry_date_match.
A longitude point filter requires latitude to be supplied.
A latitude point filter requires longitude to be supplied.
The geometry parameter accepts one or more WKT geometries.
geometry_entity applies geometries taken from specified entity identifiers.
geometry_reference applies geometries from entities matching supplied references.
geometry_curie applies geometries from entities matching supplied CURIEs.
Supported geometry relations include within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
The limit parameter controls the number of results returned.
The offset parameter controls the pagination start point.
The field parameter selects fields included in the response.
field takes precedence over exclude_field when both are supplied.
The quality parameter filters entities by recorded quality.
A specific entity can be returned as JSON, HTML or GeoJSON.
The published OpenAPI file can be used to generate a client library.
The 25cm composite DTM product is retired and no longer available as a current composite.
The retired 25cm composite has been replaced by a 1m composite product.
The survey archive still includes 25cm time-stamped data.
The retired 25cm composite was produced in 2017.
It was derived by merging and resampling the full time-stamped archive.
Where repeat surveys existed, the newest best-resolution source was selected.
The retired composite was maintained on an annual update model.
The retired DTM used the last-return LIDAR signal.
Surface objects were removed using bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
The retired 25cm DTM was distributed as ASCII files in 5km grids.
Elevation values were supplied in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The product used the OSTN15 transformation.
The stated vertical accuracy was plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
A tinted shaded-relief view was available through WMS.
Survey-index files identified the time-stamped survey used at a location.
The metadata describes airborne LIDAR acquisition at up to 500,000 measurements per second.
The open archive includes point-cloud data as well as derived raster models.
The archive contains both survey-specific products and composites of the best available data.
The metadata states no public-access constraint, subject to the identified licence.
The retired product is identified under the Open Government Licence.
The coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The metadata period begins on 1 January 1998.
The metadata period ends on 2 September 2017.
Coverage metadata was exposed through a Web Map Service.
Coverage metadata was exposed through a Web Feature Service.
OS Terrain 50 is published as both grid and contour data.
The product is supplied in multiple formats including GML, ASCII, shapefile, vector tiles and GeoPackage.
ASCII grid data is supplied alongside GML metadata.
Grid GML describes the vertical reference system.
Contour subtype names align with the draft INSPIRE elevation specification.
Terrain 50 GML explicitly declares the coordinate reference system for geometry.
Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
Metadata is available on a per-tile basis.
The metadata model includes a temporal extent for the data.
Shapefile field names are constrained to ten characters.
The shapefile abbreviation for propertyValue is PROP_VALUE.
The GML model reserves spotHeightType values for generic, form spot, mountain pass and summit classifications.
Shapefile point and line layers follow the same Terrain feature schema and can be related through geometry.
